articles.title: Sewing needles found in Halloween candy distributed in Oshawa, police say
articles.summary: Police in Durham Region are investigating after sewing needles were found in Halloween candy that was given to trick-or-treaters over the weekend. Detectives said the incident was reported in Oshawa, near Ritson Road North and Taunton Road. Officers were canvassing the area late Sunday evening. articles.title: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest champion in F1 history at age 20
articles.summary: MEXICO CITY — Twenty-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest champion in the history of Formula 1 on Sunday with four races still left in the season. articles.summary: A 40-year-old woman is facing impaired driving charges following a three-vehicle crash in Etobicoke on Sunday.

articles.title: Carney calls December byelection for Scarborough North, 5 other ridings in Canada
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has called byelections for a total of six ridings located in Saskatchewan, Ontario and Quebec that will give the Liberals a chance to strengthen their thin majority in the House of Commons.

articles.title: Pickering city council returning to in-person meetings after year-long virtual shift due to threats
articles.summary: Pickering city council is set to officially return to in-person meetings in its newly renovated council chambers on Nov. 16. after conducting municipal business online for nearly two years.

articles.title: How this Brampton community is making Halloween accessible for all kids
articles.summary: Community members in Brampton are aiming to make Halloween more accessible for children with mobility issues and other disabilities. They created a flat, low-barrier and low-sensory environment that mimicked a residential street where kids and their families could trick-or-treat and participate in activities.

articles.title: Is this Toronto's spookiest street? Meet the skeleton's of Pape Avenue
articles.summary: Houses along Pape Avenue, north of Queen East, are covered in skeletons posing in grand, creative, larger-than-life displays. CBC's Haydn Watters finds why the neighbourhood is so obsessed with skulls and bones.
